title: Evaluated trace discriminant detects an etale scheme-theoretic fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be an affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism] morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $U\subset Y$ be affine, $y\in U$, and $b$ a basis indexed by $\operatorname{Fin}(n)$ of $\Gamma(X,f^{-1}U)$ over $\Gamma(Y,U)$ via $f$. Evaluate sections at $y$ in the residue field [def-weil-residue-field] $\kappa(y)$. Then the evaluation of the trace discriminant $\det(\operatorname{Tr}(m_{b_i b_j}))$ is nonzero if and only if $X_y [def-pc-scheme-fibre]\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The case $n=0$ is included; no flatness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0BJF, discriminant-lemma-discriminant, trace-base-change and finite-dimensional fibre-algebra argument

proof.text: Identify the fibre with Spec(kappa(y) tensor_R B), using affineness. Base change the finite basis and its multiplication matrices; trace and determinant commute with evaluation. The evaluated discriminant is therefore the determinant of the fibre trace pairing. A nilpotent pairs to zero with every element, so nondegeneracy implies reduction. A reduced finite-dimensional commutative algebra is a finite product of finite field extensions; its trace pairing is their orthogonal sum and is nondegenerate precisely when every extension is separable. Finite products of finite separable extensions are exactly the etale finite algebras. Read the product argument backwards for the converse. In rank zero the determinant is one and the fibre is empty and etale. This is the remaining algebraic part of the item, independently of flatness or local lifting.

theorem trace_discriminant_evaluation_ne_zero_iff_etale_fibre
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom f]
    (U : Y.affineOpens) (y : Y) (hy : y ∈ U.1) :
    letI := (f.app U.1).hom.toAlgebra
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) Γ(Y, U.1) Γ(X, f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)),
      Y.evaluation U.1 y hy (Algebra.discr Γ(Y, U.1) b) ≠ 0 ↔
        Etale (f.fiberToSpecResidueField y)
